Integrated Management of Childhood Illness: Fever module

comparisons.claim: Classify and route under-5 cough, diarrhoea, and fever; danger signs first; possible fever at 0-59 completed days routes urgently; malaria-relevant fever uses explicit test state without medicine selection.
comparisons.codexDecision: Existing IR remains authoritative for prototype; clinician sign-off still required.

comparisons.claim: Simple watery diarrhoea can unlock ORS/zinc support; dysentery/danger signs suppress voucher; caregiver education shows ORS after each loose stool by age group and ORS until diarrhoea stops.
comparisons.codexDecision: Voucher wording is a prototype behavior-change tool and needs MOH approval.

comparisons.claim: Show clean-water, correct-volume, stir/use-same-day ORS preparation steps.
comparisons.codexDecision: Use placeholders until local ORS sachet/container photos are captured.

comparisons.claim: Brushing timer/tracker supports twice-daily fluoride toothbrushing; child amount guidance needs age/local approval.
comparisons.codexDecision: Prototype says 'small amount' and routes detailed dosing language to review.

comparisons.claim: Tooth pain, swelling, fever, bleeding, injury, and breathing/swallowing concerns route conservatively to dental/clinic/urgent care without diagnosis or treatment advice.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: checklist uses conservative Localizer routing for dental warning signs; no antibiotics, pain medicines, extraction advice, or dental diagnosis.

comparisons.claim: The recovered five-frame early reader shows dirty, sad hands seeing soap, being washed, and becoming happy, then bridges into the foreground handwashing coach.
comparisons.codexDecision: David approved restoration to the internal prototype and confirmed rights on 2026-08-07. Exact source hash, frame order, and artwork are preserved; content/local and translation review remain pending, and this is not field-use approval.

comparisons.claim: Safe-water stories support water treatment behavior and source-safety awareness, then bridge into the safe-water checker, boil-water timer, and local cholera alert tools.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: story summary is adapted, not copied; action buttons are education-to-tool navigation only and local WASH wording/assets are required.

comparisons.claim: The recovered five-frame early reader shows a sad tooth finding a toothbrush, being brushed, and becoming happy, then bridges into the brushing coach and tooth-pain check.
comparisons.codexDecision: David approved restoration to the internal prototype and confirmed rights on 2026-08-07. Exact source hash, frame order, and artwork are preserved; content/local and translation review remain pending, and this is not field-use approval.

comparisons.claim: A fictional story about diarrhoeal germs spreading through unsafe water, contaminated hands, food, flies, and open defecation, and WASH practices presented as prevention lessons.
comparisons.codexDecision: David approved restoration to the internal prototype and confirmed rights on 2026-08-07. Content/local review is required for chlorine, boiling, filtering, sanitation, and diarrhoeal-prevention wording; translation review also remains pending. This is not field-use approval.

comparisons.claim: Cold and flu stories reinforce handwashing and cough-covering habits, then bridge into handwashing practice and the under-5 sick-child cough check without replacing clinical fever/ARI triage.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: story summary is adapted, not copied; action buttons are education-to-tool navigation only. Cough preselection opens relevant triage questions but does not evaluate, diagnose, or imply flu.

comparisons.claim: ANC reminders and birth plan support timely pregnancy care and preparedness.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: prototype supports birth preparedness checklist items but generates no clinical schedule until local ANC schedule is approved.

comparisons.claim: Postpartum and lactation danger checklist conservatively routes separate caregiver-visible danger findings such as heavy bleeding, large clots, placenta or membrane pieces after birth, bad-smelling discharge, breathing or chest symptoms, severe headache or vision changes, severe belly pain, severe swelling of face/hands/legs, newborn poor feeding, and thoughts of harm or feeling unsafe to urgent care, urgent newborn care, or trusted emergency/crisis support.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: CDC Hear Her and WHO postnatal guidance are adapted into postpartum/lactation referral support; local maternity, newborn, lactation, safeguarding, and crisis pathways must replace draft wording before release.

comparisons.claim: Breastfeeding aid and triage combines newborn danger screening, maternal postpartum danger screening, feeding-intake concerns, attachment pain concerns, and exclusive-breastfeeding counselling into one prototype aid surface, adapted from the breastfeeding lessons zip and routed conservatively through the existing screen-card clinical IR.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: the zip's useful questions and counselling are adapted for an internal prototype only. Contract extensions, dyad storage, validated thresholds, translations, and local lactation pathways remain unresolved.

comparisons.claim: Breastfeeding audio help supports positioning, attachment/latch support, feeding cues, on demand feeding, and referral for difficulty or danger signs.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: audio helper scripts are placeholders and must be reviewed by local lactation/newborn clinicians.

comparisons.claim: Prototype vaccine reminders may calculate the next WHO-style routine visit from a child's birth date, but real reminders must follow the approved local EPI schedule and the child's vaccine card/clinic record.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: WHO-style prototype date calculation is allowed for demo; exact local EPI table, clinic record, and vaccine card must control field use.

comparisons.claim: Zinc course tracker supports remembering a 10-day prototype course alongside ORS/fluids for childhood diarrhoea, shows WHO-style age quantities, and explains dissolving a local dispersible zinc dose in clean water or breastmilk.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: 10-day synthetic tracker and WHO-style prototype quantities only; local zinc product/clinician instructions control dose form and duration, and diarrhoea danger signs override.

comparisons.claim: Handwashing timer supports a 20-second soap-and-water habit with story/game reinforcement.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: coach provides foreground 20-second behavior support for soap, lathering all hand surfaces, rinsing, and drying; no sleeping-phone reminder reliability is assumed.

comparisons.claim: Chlorine-treated water should stand before use; dosage must come from product/local guidance.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: timer shows foreground wait concept and intentionally omits dose until local chlorine table is approved; no sleeping-phone alert is assumed.

comparisons.claim: Boiling water panel supports rolling-boil timing and clean covered storage education.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: prototype uses a foreground 1-minute rolling-boil helper, names the 3-minute high-elevation exception, and defers to local public-health advisories.

comparisons.claim: Hotspot alert prioritizes safe water, handwashing, sanitation, ORS readiness, and urgent care for dehydration during cholera/diarrhoea risk.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: alert checklist covers WASH, ORS readiness, clinic contact, and urgent dehydration care; local outbreak authority controls timing and wording, and WAP background alerts are not assumed.

comparisons.claim: KMC tracker supports skin-to-skin session tracking for preterm/low-birth-weight babies under health-worker guidance.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: KMC timer records synthetic skin-to-skin minutes only; health-worker guidance, newborn danger signs, and facility care override the timer.

comparisons.claim: Newborn danger checklist conservatively routes not feeding/poor feeding, difficult or fast breathing/chest indrawing, fever/too hot/too cold, no movement/reduced activity/floppy or convulsions, and yellow palms/soles or worsening jaundice concern to urgent newborn care now; small or early baby concerns route to same-day health-worker or facility support.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: WHO and UNICEF newborn danger-sign language is adapted into referral support only; local newborn clinicians must approve wording, thresholds, and referral pathways before release.

comparisons.claim: Pregnancy danger checklist conservatively routes bleeding or fluid leaking, severe headache/vision change, dizziness/fainting/swelling, trouble breathing/chest pain/fast heartbeat, severe belly pain, fever, severe vomiting/unable to drink, baby movement stopping or slowing, and thoughts of harm or feeling unsafe to urgent care or trusted emergency support.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: CDC Hear Her and WHO ANC danger-sign phrasing are adapted into an urgent-routing checklist; local maternity, emergency, safeguarding, and crisis-support pathways must replace draft wording before release.

comparisons.claim: Kohl/kajal screen flags child, pregnancy/nursing, and unknown/imported product exposure; advises stopping use, keeping products from children, and asking a healthcare provider about blood lead testing.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: FDA and CDC lead-exposure guidance is used as a prototype safety screen pending local toxicology/public-health review; the app does not identify safe products or diagnose lead poisoning.

comparisons.claim: Vision screen points caregivers toward a screening or eye exam when a child has repeated seeing concerns such as squinting, eye rubbing/discomfort, headaches or trouble after reading/schoolwork, or caregiver/teacher concern; sudden vision change, eye injury, or severe eye pain route to urgent care.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: this is a referral-support checklist, not a vision test or diagnosis; urgent-eye wording and local eye-care pathways need local review.

comparisons.claim: Hearing screen supports referral after caregiver/teacher/child concern, speech or language concern, failed hearing screen, or missing follow-up; infant follow-up preserves CDC EHDI 1-3-6 benchmarks.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: this is a referral-support checklist, not a hearing test or diagnosis; local hearing-screening/audiology pathways and infant follow-up wording need review.

comparisons.claim: Household preparedness checklist supports clinic contact, transport, ORS, safe water, and medicine refill planning.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: offline non-clinical readiness checklist for water/ORS, clinic and emergency contacts, transport, documents, medicines/refills, and family meet-up plan; local emergency/referral pathways must replace draft wording.

comparisons.claim: Quality console surfaces source coverage, prototype status, memory profile, and CODEX Decision items for review.
comparisons.codexDecision: Console is an internal review tool and not caregiver content.

comparisons.claim: Learning-signals dashboard is ethics-gated and synthetic-only until review, consent, security, and export governance are approved.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: no real research participant data can be collected in this prototype.

comparisons.claim: Routine postnatal reminders should use an approved local schedule and point urgent concerns to danger checks.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: prototype plans mother/newborn follow-up readiness but calculates no visit dates until an exact local PNC schedule is approved.

comparisons.claim: Medicine refill tracker supports a private calendar reminder and an optional session-only reference photo of a medicine box, prescription, or bottle, without dose advice or medicine changes.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: calendar reminder and optional session-only reference photo only; it does not calculate doses, start/stop/split/change medicines, judge adherence, retain a medicine list, or replace clinician/pharmacist review.

comparisons.claim: Labor clock records locally approved timing threshold and transport buffer only; pregnancy danger signs override planned timing.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: local threshold, native alarm reliability, SMS fallback, and maternity referral pathway are required before real use.

comparisons.claim: Bednet reminder supports hanging, checking, repairing, and prioritizing insecticide-treated nets for pregnant people and children where malaria risk exists.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: prevention reminder only; fever or suspected malaria must follow local malaria testing and treatment guidance.

comparisons.claim: Dehydration guide starts with danger signs and routes inability to drink, sunken eyes, lethargy, repeated vomiting, or worsening illness to urgent care; ORS support remains only when the child can drink.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: text-only guide pending image work; it is not a diagnosis or dehydration classification.

comparisons.claim: Plain-language first-foods guide explains that at about 6 months breastfed children keep breastfeeding while adding 2 or 3 spoonfuls of thick, soft food twice a day, then adding varied safe local foods over time; it also covers patient, non-forcing feeding and clean hands, water, bowl, and spoon.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: guidance-first education followed by an optional plan; local nutrition counseling, food availability, translation, and growth-faltering protocols control.

comparisons.claim: Chlorine dose helper echoes user-entered local product/table dose and water volume; it does not generate a dose from generic constants.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: local table required; helper does not invent, interpolate, or endorse a chlorine dose.

comparisons.claim: Sanitation checklist supports latrine use, handwashing access, child feces disposal, cleaning supplies, and local WASH contact while keeping diarrhoea danger routing visible.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: WASH checklist only; local sanitation program guidance and diarrhoea danger signs override.

comparisons.claim: Ear problem check asks about ear pain, ear discharge, and tender swelling behind the ear; swelling behind the ear routes urgently and pain/discharge route to same-day clinic or health-worker care without antibiotics, ear drops, or diagnosis.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: WHO IMCI ear-problem structure is adapted into referral support only; local child-health clinicians must approve wording, thresholds, and care pathway.

comparisons.claim: Measles rash check asks about fever/spreading rash with cough, runny nose, or red watery eyes, and routes suspected signs to clinic or health worker today; eye or mouth complications, danger signs, or breathing concern route urgently.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: CDC measles signs and WHO IMCI measles complication framing are adapted into conservative routing; local outbreak notification, immunization, isolation, and referral wording must replace draft copy.

comparisons.claim: MUAC nutrition screen uses local MUAC tape red/yellow color flags, bilateral foot swelling, visible wasting/weight loss, and appetite concern to route children to nutrition or clinic care without calculating malnutrition or giving feeding treatment.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: UNICEF child-wasting and WHO IMCI nutrition classification concepts are adapted into referral support; local nutrition program thresholds, RUTF/feeding protocols, and growth-monitoring workflows control.

comparisons.claim: Child injury first-aid check routes unconsciousness, breathing trouble, seizure, serious bleeding, serious burn, broken-bone concern, severe head-injury symptoms, poisoning, drowning, or electrocution to urgent or emergency help without teaching treatment steps.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: CDC HEADS UP and NHS first aid are used only for emergency-sign routing; local emergency numbers, first-aid training, transport pathways, and safeguarding rules must replace draft copy.

comparisons.claim: Channel twins preview shows how one approved module message could render as app card, SMS, IVR, WhatsApp, and CHW script variants while keeping sensitive-content and privacy review visible.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: WHO digital interventions support targeted client communication only under implementation, privacy, and health-system capacity conditions; this prototype creates no live SMS, IVR, WhatsApp, or CHW outbound message.

comparisons.claim: Referral follow-up queue models a closed-loop service task for danger screens, ORS voucher support, contact attempt, unresolved status, and closure notes using synthetic data only.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: closed-loop referral follow-up requires defined CHW scope, call/visit scripts, supervisor escalation, facility feedback, and data-sharing agreements before real use.

comparisons.claim: Shared phone privacy mode prepares quick hide, private labels, notification wording, opt-out, local-only storage, and user-owned export checks before sensitive module expansion.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: UNICEF Responsible Data for Children principles are adapted as design prompts only; no hidden sync, real sensitive storage, or production notification behavior is approved.

comparisons.claim: Partner service dashboard summarizes aggregate synthetic source approval, language readiness, unresolved referral, channel performance, and service feedback indicators.
comparisons.codexDecision: CODEX Decision - needs approval: aggregate only; no individual surveillance dashboard, production analytics, role-based access, or partner reporting without server, security, governance, and data-sharing review.
